topic: 3 Days Left: Final Submission Checklist for Stage 2

messages.content:
Dear participants,

We hope you have enjoyed exploring the autoformalization of equational theories in Lean 4 through the Mathematics Distillation Challenge - Stage 2.

Around three days remain until the submission ends. Here is a final checklist before the submission deadline:

1. Submit through the SAIR competition platform

Please submit your final solver through the competition platform:
https://competition.sair.foundation/competitions/mathematics-distillation-challenge-equational-theories-stage2/overview

Do not submit through the Playground. The Playground is for testing only, and submissions made there will not count as official competition submissions.

When submitting:

  • Select your track: Solo or Marathon.
  • Select your model: gemma4-31b or gpt-oss-120b.
  • Each participant may submit up to four solvers in total.
  • Final results will be reported on four separate leaderboards, one for each track-model combination.

Please also use the Submission Note to provide relevant details:

  • If your solver includes compressed data or binary blobs, describe what they contain and how they were generated.
  • If your submission draws on work from the Contributor Network or another open-source project, please identify the source.

2. Test your solvers

The Playground may be busy as the deadline approaches. For faster testing and iteration, we recommend setting up the Lean 4 environment locally.

The evaluation environment uses Lean v4.33.1 and Mathlib v4.33.1.

Evaluation specifications:
https://playground.sair.foundation/playground/mathematics-distillation-challenge-equational-theories-stage2/official-evaluation-spec

Official repository:
https://github.com/SAIRcompetition/equational-theories-lean-stage2

3. Review the test datasets

Reference problems are available on Hugging Face:
https://huggingface.co/datasets/SAIRfoundation/equational-theories-selected-problems

We have also prepared a Stage 2 stress-test dataset containing 200 problems across four categories:

  • order4_normal
  • order4_hard
  • order4_extra_hard
  • order5_normal

Each category contains 50 problems: 25 true and 25 false. Each problem is worth one point. The final main leaderboard evaluation will use the same category distribution and scoring configuration.

Stage 2 stress-test dataset:
https://huggingface.co/datasets/SAIRfoundation/equational-theories-selected-problems/viewer/stage2_stress_test

Some participants have already achieved 100% accuracy on the standard problem sets, so we have also prepared an experimental order5_hard dataset for further research and testing. Some problems have unknown ground truth, and this dataset will not be used for the main leaderboard.

Experimental Order-5 Hard dataset:
https://huggingface.co/datasets/SAIRfoundation/equational-theories-selected-problems/viewer/research_order5_hard

Thank you for supporting SAIR Competitions and for all the excellent suggestions and feedback. Community feedback continues to drive our work.

We also welcome you to join our upcoming competitions. The Lean Kernel Challenge, co-organized with Lean FRO, will officially launch on September 15.

Enjoy the competition, and good luck with your submissions! :tada:

messages.content: Thanks for organizing! One question on evaluation, how will you rank tied solvers? Is total/avg time the best metric? I am having a hard time choosing between optimizing for time or generalization strength. I also published a solver on the contribution network (claudev5) , it is 100% accurate on the current Playground problem set.
